name: Abdullah ibn Wahb
nameAr: عبد الله بن وهب بن مسلم القرشي الفهري مولاهم المصري

nisbas.en: a client (mawla) of Banu Fihr, so counted with them by clientage, not descent

taqrib.en: Reliable, a hadith master and devout worshipper.

role: Jurist of Egypt; Malik's student and the main carrier of Egyptian and Hijazi hadith

teachers.name: Hammad ibn Zayd
teachers.source: reciprocal of the entry in hammad-ibn-zayd's record (Tahdhib al-Tahdhib)

verdicts.ar: عبد الله بن وهب صحيح الحديث، يفصل السماع من العرض والحديث من الحديث، ما أصح حديثه وأثبته
verdicts.en: Abdullah ibn Wahb is sound in hadith; he distinguishes what he heard from what was read to him, and one report from another. How sound and firm his hadith is! Told that he was lax in how he received, he said: he was, but when you examine his hadith and what he transmits from his teachers you find it sound.

verdicts.ar: نظرت في نحو ثلاثين ألف حديث من حديث ابن وهب بمصر وغير مصر، لا أعلم أني رأيت له حديثا لا أصل له، وهو ثقة
verdicts.en: I examined about thirty thousand of Ibn Wahb's hadith, in Egypt and elsewhere, and I do not know that I saw one without a basis. He is reliable.

verdicts.ar: صالح الحديث، صدوق، أحب إلي من الوليد بن مسلم، وأصح حديثا منه بكثير
verdicts.en: Acceptable in hadith, truthful; dearer to me than al-Walid ibn Muslim and far sounder in hadith than he.

verdicts.ar: كان كثير العلم، ثقة فيما قال: حدثنا، وكان يدلس
verdicts.en: He was of abundant learning, reliable in what he introduced with 'he narrated to us'; and he would use the ambiguous formula (tadlis).

verdicts.ar: كان يتساهل في الأخذ، ولا بأس به. وقال في موضع آخر: ثقة، ما أعلمه روى عن الثقات حديثا منكرا
verdicts.en: He was lax in how he received hadith, but there is no harm in him. Elsewhere: reliable; I know of no objectionable hadith he transmitted from reliable narrators.

verdicts.ar: عبد الله بن وهب من أجلة الناس ومن ثقاتهم، وحديث الحجاز ومصر وما والى تلك البلاد يدور على رواية ابن وهب
verdicts.en: Among the most eminent and reliable of people; the hadith of the Hijaz and Egypt and the lands adjoining them turns on Ibn Wahb's transmission.

dhahabi.source: al-Kashif, as quoted on the Shamela narrator record

tadlis.source: Ibn Hajar, Ta'rif Ahl al-Taqdis bi-Maratib al-Mawsufin bi-l-Tadlis (Tabaqat al-Mudallisin), entry 17, first rank: described as a mudallis by Ibn Sa'd in the Tabaqat
tadlis.note: The first rank holds those found to have used the ambiguous formula only rarely. In al-Bukhari 71 his link to Yunus reads 'from' (عن يونس); in Muslim 1037, through Harmala, he says 'Yunus informed me' (أخبرني يونس).

flags.label: Lax in the manner of receiving
flags.detail: Ahmad and al-Nasa'i note that he was easy-going about how he received hadith (al-Saji explains that his countrymen accepted licence, ijaza, and would say 'he narrated to me' of it). Both nonetheless judged what he actually transmitted to be sound, and Ahmad praised him for distinguishing hearing from reading-back in his formulae.

bio: The jurist of Egypt in the generation after al-Layth ibn Sa'd, a student of Malik and of the Egyptian and Hijazi masters, and the person through whom most of their hadith reached later collectors. Al-Bukhari and Muslim both rely on him heavily. Ibn Hajar places him in the first and lightest rank of those who used the ambiguous formula, so a bare 'from' in his chains is not held against him.

provenance.ref: Shamela narrator record 3976, drawing on Tahdhib al-Kamal 16/277 and Tahdhib al-Tahdhib 2/453
